commits.message:
[BAKCEND] Fix FP4 TMA descriptor selection for small block K (#11935)

Mixed FP8/FP4 matmuls with BLOCK_K=32 or 64 can propagate an MMA-only
padded shared-memory layout into a TMA descriptor. Reject unsupported
padded layouts during descriptor selection, including shared_linear
candidate matching, so these cases load packed bytes with a valid TMA
layout and convert to the existing MMA layout.

Add small-BLOCK_K coverage to the FP8/FP4 TMA matmul test and compiler
regressions for direct and shared_linear consumers. Validated on GB300:
all 36 TMA matmul cases pass, and the descriptor-encoding lit test
passes.

Related to #11930.

commits.message:
[triton_kernels] Fix gathered activation scale indexing (#11928)

When a ragged matmul gathers activation rows, the values can use a dense
TMA descriptor while their scales are stored in padded, per-slice
blocks.
Selecting scale offsets from the values' descriptor mode uses a dense
row
count that is undefined for ragged inputs, causing compilation to fail.

Select scale offsets using the matmul's ragged dimension. Require the
scale layout and matmul to share the same `RaggedTensorMetadata`
instance
so their row boundaries and padding agree, without synchronizing device
data on each call. Document this contract and the required scale row
order
for gathered inputs.

## Validation

- Added four cases to `test_gathered_ragged_act_scale_indexing` in
`python/triton_kernels/tests/test_matmul.py`: shared metadata, different
  block offsets, different row boundaries with identical block offsets,
  and separately created metadata with equal contents.
- Reproduced the original compilation failure and the missing metadata
  validation before the fixes. All four cases pass with the fixes on
  NVIDIA GB200.
- 56 additional GB200 checks passed, covering gathered inputs, uneven
and
  empty slices, strided scales, and dense, batched, and ragged layouts.
- `pre-commit run --from-ref origin/main --to-ref HEAD` passed.

`python/triton_kernels/tests/test_matmul.py`.

commits.comment: 为 GSan 增加 write-once 分配模式：将原来的单一 reserved 区域拆成两个 1 TiB arena（由地址位 kArenaSize 区分 normal/write-once），write-once shadow cell 简化为单个 ScalarClock（4 字节，为普通 ShadowCell 的 1/6），granularity 从 4 字节降到 1 字节（byte-granularity），因此 shadow 内存占用反而更小，且访问无需 rwLock，完全 wait-free。GSan.h 增加 getShadowGranularity/getShadowCellSize/getRealCapacity、isWriteOnceAddress、categorize(AddressCategory)，GSanLibrary.cu 增加 doWrite/doRead/checkAtomicAddress(禁止 write-once 上的 atomic)、以及 roundRange 支持可配置 granularity；违反 write-once 规则（二次写、首次写前读、跨界访问、atomic 访问）会触发 assert。GSanAllocator.cc 把 treeRoot 改为 treeRoots[2]，gsanMalloc/export/import 增加 write_once 参数，新增 is_write_once_allocation API。python/triton/experimental/gsan/_allocator.py 与 symmetric_memory.py 增加 write_once 参数与校验，_testing_utils 用 shadow_granularity/shadow_cell_size 动态查询替换常量。新增 test_write_once.py 与 test_write_once_failures.py 大量测试。风险点：GSanAllocator 的 pyMalloc/export/import 的 Python 参数个数放宽（2-4/2-3/5-6），新增 is_write_once_allocation METH_O，这些是 GSan 内部接口，不涉及 Ascend。

commits.message:
[GSan] Add write_once allocations (#11774)

This adds a special "write-once" gsan allocation. The rules here are
that they can be written exactly once, and read many times after being
written.

This means we only need to track for read-after-write violations, so we
can simplify the shadow cell to a single scalar write clock which is
1/6th of the size of a normal shadow cell. This allows us to track
byte-granularity while actually using less shadow memory than 4-byte
granularity normal allocations.

Also, this allows for a completely wait-free shadow memory access
pattern. This means we don't serialize accesses to those address.

Closes #11753

I got codex to port the llvm back into inline asm which reverted some of
the slow down. It also found a more efficient mechanism for fp32 to fp8

quite as bad. BF16 actually improved vs main.

commits.message:
Disable floating-point fusion by default (#11270)

Disable implicit floating-point fusion by default. Kernels can opt in
with
enable_fp_fusion=True, or applications can restore the previous default
with TRITON_DEFAULT_FP_FUSION=1.

Set TRITON_FORCE_DISABLE_FP_FUSION=1 before starting the process to
override both settings. Explicit tl.fma operations remain fused.

Preserve fusion-dependent arithmetic with explicit FMAs and targeted
kernel opt-ins. Enable fusion for the Hopper MXFP4 test because a ptxas
bug causes it to fail with fusion disabled.

commits.comment: 【意图】修复 loop scheduler 把 load 放到循环内 `gdc_wait()` 之前的错误，使 PDL 消费者可能在生产者写完数据前读取数据（issue #11905）。【实现】在 lib/Dialect/TritonGPU/Transforms/Pipeliner/ScheduleLoops.cpp 的 `isSafeToPipeline(scf::ForOp)` 中，将 `tt::GridDependencyWaitOp` 加入 `containsAny` 检查，与 `ttg::BarrierOp`、`tt::AssertOp`、`tt::PrintOp` 一样被视作阻断流水化的 op；含 gdc_wait 的循环保持非流水化状态，而 wait 发生在循环之前则不影响循环本身的流水化。实现方式沿用了已有的 containsAny 模板检测，改动仅两行，属同一机制的语义扩展。【风险】低。语义上收紧了可流水化的循环集合（可能牺牲部分含 GDC wait 循环的性能），但正确性优先；对不含 GDC 的循环无行为变化。测试覆盖了三种典型场景（循环内 wait、循环内 if 内 wait、循环前 wait），并明确断言前两者不出现 `loop.stage` 属性、后者正常流水化。

ascend_impact.functionality: 无影响。该变更只修改 lib/Dialect/TritonGPU/Transforms/Pipeliner/ScheduleLoops.cpp 的循环流水化安全判定；triton-ascend 走 TritonToLinalg 转换链，不使用 TritonGPU Pipeliner 与 loop.stage 调度属性，因此不影响 AscendBackend 的 add_stages、Ascend 的 lowering 或 NPUDriver 行为。
ascend_impact.testing: 无影响。triton-ascend 无对应的 TritonGPU pipeline 调度测试；本次新增的 test/TritonGPU/pipeline-schedule-loop.mlir 用例属上游 lit 测试，不参与 Ascend 构建与运行。

commits.message:
[PIPELINE] Keep dependent loads after GDC waits (#11906)

The loop scheduler can place a load before an in-loop `gdc_wait()`,
allowing a PDL consumer to read data before its producer has finished
writing it.

Treat GDC waits like CTA barriers when deciding whether to pipeline a
loop. Loops containing a wait remain unpipelined; waiting before the
loop still allows pipelining.

Fixes #11905.

Implemented with Codex assistance.

commits.message:
[Frontend] Fix constexprs being prematurely to_tensor'd (#11913)

Our promotion rules state that a runtime value with an existing dtype
should take precedence over a constexpr value's inferred dtype. However,
by calling to_tensor before we pass the constexpr to semantic, this
context is lost and we may over-promote.

commits.message:
[Build][NFC] Upgrade to C++20 & use some new features (#11920)

Closes #11505

affected_interfaces: CMakeLists.txt (CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 17→20, removal of -std=gnu++17 flag, MLIR/LLVM include dirs changed to SYSTEM)
triton-ascend C++ backend sources (third_party/ascend/lib/, third_party/ascend/ascend_ir.cc, triton_ascend.cc, etc.) — now compiled under C++20
deep_analysis.adaptation_guide: This is an NFC build/toolchain commit with no changes to any of the interface_surface seams (BaseBackend/DriverBase/TritonSemantic/CodeGenerator/compiler.parse/TritonOpBuilder/InterpreterBuilder are all untouched). The C++20 migration is mechanical: `.count()`/`.find()==end()` → `.contains()`, and a custom `BitCast` → `std::bit_cast`, all in files that triton-ascend's release patch does NOT modify (except CMakeLists.txt). Adaptation is limited to: (1) resolving the merge conflict in CMakeLists.txt when cherry-picking — triton-ascend's patch adds ~55 lines to CMakeLists.txt and the commit modifies the same regions (`set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 17)`, the `-std=gnu++17` flag line, and the `include_directories(${MLIR_INCLUDE_DIRS}/${LLVM_INCLUDE_DIRS})` block); ensure triton-ascend's added CMake content (e.g. third_party/ascend subdirectory registration, any added compiler flags) is reconciled with `CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 20`/`CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON` and does not re-add a hardcoded `-std=gnu++17`. (2) Rebuild and verify triton-ascend's own C++ code compiles under C++20 — most C++17 code is C++20-compatible, but check for `-Wambiguous-reversed-operator` warnings in triton-ascend's own headers (LLVM/MLIR headers are now SYSTEM includes, but triton-ascend headers are not) and for any use of removed/deprecated C++17 features. No source-level interface changes are required.
